text:
Tara: Ran a KV-window reclaim experiment on staging with the new compact-pass enabled. Seeing ~12% p99 latency regression and noticeable GPU memory thrash when compact cycles align with a burst of short requests. Posting quick traces and perf samples.

Mike: Can you paste the perf counters and kernel-selection logs? want to see if fallback happened during reclaim.

Tara: Quick gist of what I ran:
```bash
./run_staging_experiment --profile=kv-reclaim --compact-mode=aggressive --runtime-opts=kv_window=64
```
Perf snippet (top hot functions, sampled at 1ms):
```
  34%  runtime.so     paged_block_compact
  18%  runtime.so     kv_insert_path
  12%  kernels.ptx    attention_small_block_kernel
  10%  kernels.ptx    attention_large_block_kernel
  07%  runtime.so     workspace_alloc
```
Also saw a short sequence where the kernel selector switched from "large_block" -> "small_block" for ~120ms concurrent with compaction.

perf-bot: perf-runner: job kv-window-reclaim-staging-204567 finished. artifacts: s3://perf/artifacts/kv-reclaim/204567. flamegraph + timeline uploaded.

Jess: :thinking: My hunch is batching heuristic + workspace sizing are interacting — when batcher coalesces lots of short-seq requests, the block reuse ratio drops and we trigger more compactions. compaction cost then forces kernel fallback which hurts throughput.

Anita: Agree. Two quick knobs to try: increase per-stream max_live_blocks, and add a small delay to compaction scans (defer window by ~100ms) so compactions don't hit hot bursts. Also consider forcing kernel-selection preference on reclaim path to avoid expensive fallback thrash.

Mike: Test plan (overnight):
  1) bump block_size target from 256->384 for the reclaim path only
  2) cap concurrent compactions to 2
  3) jitter compaction scan by 50-150ms
  4) force kernel_selector.prefer="small_block" during reclaim to compare
I'll run A/B against baseline and attach token-level latency + GPU mem curves.

Tara: Sweet, thanks. I'll add a small repro that creates short bursts to try to deterministically surface the compaction alignment.

Jess: :thumbsup:

Tara: attaching short memory timeline dump (simplified):
```text
time(ms)  live_blocks  free_blocks  compactions_active  p99(ms)
0         120          400          0                   18
40        180          340          1                   22
90        95           425          2                   27  <-- compaction + kernel switch
150       210          310          1                   20
```

Mike: If the A/B shows reduced p99 and less kernel switching, next step is to codify reclaim jitter and a temporary 'no-compact' window during high-concurrency bursts.

Tara: noted. I'll upload the deterministic repro and baseline flamegraphs tomorrow morning. Thanks all.
